A plan for African Ancestry.

Prepared for Gina Paige · September 2026

Dario Calmese · Calvary Rogers · Obed Appiah-Agyeman

Open simply. This is a plan for the next chapter of African Ancestry: what is holding the business back today, how we fix it, and how the story she has built for 23 years becomes a system that keeps families coming back. The look of this deck is the look we propose for the brand.
02 / 19

Where we stand

Four things are holding you back.

01

Your ads can't see your sales.

In August, Meta ads got the same clicks as July and reported half the purchases.

02

Search and AI can't read your site.

Your home and product pages load empty for them.

03

The site undersells a $299 test.

Price, timing, and your privacy promise are hard to find.

04

Most revenue ends at one sale.

71% of revenue comes from first-time buyers.

Four problems, in plain terms. One: the ads still work, but Meta can't see most of the sales they drive. July and August had the same clicks; Meta reported half the purchases. These are Meta's figures, not total sales. Two: search engines and AI assistants see an empty page on the home and product pages, because the content only appears after code runs in the browser. Three: the pages after the click don't make the case for a $299 test. Price, results timing and the privacy promise are hard to find. Four: most revenue is a single sale. 71% of revenue comes from first-time buyers, and 95% of sales are test kits.

What's causing it

Your site today, on a phone.

01

Checkout leaves your site.

Meta loses track of the sale.

02

What search and AI see.

An empty page until code runs.

03

A popup covers Add to cart.

Results timing: three answers.

04

Reviews stop in 2023.

Nothing brings people back.

What we found on the live site on 25 September, at phone size. One: the checkout moves to africanancestry.myshopify.com, and the Add to cart signal never reaches Meta, so Meta loses the trail before the sale. Two: this is the product page as search engines and AI assistants see it. Everything loads later, in the browser. Three: an SMS popup lands on the product page right at Add to cart, and results timing appears three different ways across the site. Four: the newest reviews on the product page, sorted most recent, are from 2023. After the result arrives, there is nothing to come back to.

23 years, over a million people served

Positions are our read of each company's offer.

Two questions. Left to right: what a customer learns, region percentages or a people and a place. Bottom to top: what happens after the result, a one-time report or a lifelong family. 23andMe, Living DNA and AfroRoots sell percentages, once. Ancestry sells percentages but keeps people with its records. African Ancestry today sits bottom right: the most specific answer anyone offers, delivered once. The top right is empty. A specific answer that becomes a lifelong family relationship is somewhere no competitor can go, because only she has the database, the specificity, the privacy promise, and 23 years of trust with over a million people.
05 / 19

How we fix it

Five moves.

See every sale

Meta and Shopify count the same purchases.

Be found

Search engines and AI assistants can read and recommend you.

Sell with clarity

Price, timing, and your privacy promise on the first screen.

Tell one story everywhere

The same look and voice across site, ads, email, and checkout.

Give the story a home

A family app that brings people back after the result.

Five moves, one per problem, plus the one that ties them together. See every sale: fix the measurement so Meta counts what Shopify counts. Be found: make the site readable to search engines and AI assistants. Sell with clarity: put price, timing and the privacy promise on the first screen, with no popups in the way. Tell one story everywhere: one look and voice from the ad to the checkout. And give the story a home: a family app, so the relationship continues after the result.
06 / 19

The core problem

Your story has always driven your sales.

What's been missing is a system to hold it, and catalyze its value.

This is the heart of it. The reveals, the families, the celebrities, the founders: her story has always been what sells the test. But there has never been a system to hold that story after the sale, or to turn it into more value for her and for families. Everything that follows builds that system.

Four milestones, no dates. Each one pays off on its own and sets up the next. One, stabilize: Meta sees every sale and search engines can read the site, so the ad budget works at full strength again. Two, relaunch the storefront on mobile and desktop, with ad to checkout in three taps, so more of the people who click actually buy. Three, open the family app: Discover, Preserve, Connect and Pass on, so customers come back after the result and families trace the next line. Four, grow beyond the family into communities, institutions and the diaspora, for new audiences and contracts instead of one sale at a time. We start with the first: stabilize, because everything else depends on it.

Milestone one is plumbing, and it comes first because everything else depends on it. Keep checkout on her own web address, send Add to cart and purchases to Meta, keep the click ID on every ad link, and make every page readable to search and AI. Then a weekly scorecard of five numbers, so she can watch it work. When Meta can see every step of a sale, it learns who her buyers are and finds more people like them. The same budget works harder.

Milestone 02 · Relaunch the storefront

Brings back: more buyers per click

Price and privacy up front Checkout in three taps A page for every ad
Milestone two is the storefront, desktop and mobile, in the language you're looking at. The first screen says what she does, shows the price and results timing, and carries the privacy promise. The product page makes the case for $299 before anyone scrolls. No banners or popups between the ad and the checkout, and every ad gets a page that continues its story. Some photos are stand-ins until we shoot real families.

Milestone 02 · The wait and the reveal

Make the wait part of the story.

Brings back: reveals that get shared

01

While you wait

Track the kit to the lab. Each week, a short read and a prompt to record an elder.

02

Ready when you are

Results arrive sealed. Open them now, or plan a reveal with family.

03

The reveal

A people and a place, told like a story, with a page worth sharing.

Results take six to eight weeks after the lab receives the swab. We'd make that time part of the story. While you wait: the app tracks the kit from delivery to the lab, and each week brings a short read and a prompt to record an elder, so the family archive starts before the result arrives. It's also the natural moment to offer the next line. Ready when you are: results arrive sealed. Customers can open them alone, or plan a family reveal and invite relatives to open it together, in person or on a call. The reveal itself tells a people and a place like a story, and ends on a page worth sharing, with permission. Every shared reveal is a story for the ads, and every relative in the room is a possible next test.

Milestone 03 · Open the family app

A home for the story.

Brings back: customers who return after the result
Milestone three is the family app, and it's where the story finally has a home. Discover is the result itself: your people and your place. Preserve is the family archive, voices, photos and recipes, because so much of this history was never written down. Connect brings people together: members who share your line, events in your city, journeys home. Pass on gives the next generation their story. Elders and newborns join free, so the family grows from both ends. This is what brings customers back after the result, and leads each person to trace their next line.

Where the revenue goes long term. Today 95% of sales are test kits and 71% of revenue comes from first-time buyers: a one-time business. Next, the test becomes the way in. Everyone has four grandparent lines, and about 60% of returning customers already buy another kit, so the next line is the first new stream. Then family membership, heirlooms like books and certificates, experiences like events and travel home, and institutional contracts. The new numbers to watch are ongoing revenue per family, and monthly active use of the app. We haven't attached prices to any of these yet; that comes after she tells us what resonates.

Family seasons

How the system changes her ads. The goal moves from one test sale to a family that stays. The story moves from celebrity and brand moments to members' own reveals, shared with their permission; the app produces those every day. Every ad lands on a page that continues its story, not a generic product page. The audience grows to include members' families and each member's next line. And the measure becomes ongoing revenue per family, not only the purchases Meta can see. Three campaigns we'd run first: reveal stories, your next line, and family seasons around her biggest months: February, Black Friday, and Juneteenth.

This builds one layer per click, as a shape rather than a forecast. It starts from today: 71% of revenue from first-time buyers and 29% from returning customers, with the seasonal peaks she already has. The dashed line is today's path. Click one, milestones one and two: stabilizing and the new storefront recover what's already there, so the same clicks turn into more first-time sales. Click two, the family app: families come back for the next line, seats and the archive. About 60% of returning customers already buy another kit, so this is the layer that grows most. Click three, beyond the family: new streams arrive in steps, through contracts with institutions and communities. The point is the shape: growth that compounds instead of starting over every month. We'll set real targets with her numbers.
